title: Immutability
concept: Immutability is the pattern of creating a new copy instead of directly modifying data

steps.title: Mutable approach: direct mutation
steps.explanation:
Directly modifying user.age.
The original object is changed.

steps.title: Immutable approach: preserving the original
steps.explanation:
Creating the user2 object.
This object will not be modified.

steps.title: Immutable approach: creating a new object
steps.explanation:
Spread to copy, then override just age.
The original `user2` is untouched — a **New Identity** object is created on the Heap.
steps.analogy: Instead of using correction fluid on the original document, you copy it to a new sheet, make your changes, and submit the new version.

steps.title: Checking the original
steps.explanation:
user2.age is still 25.
The original has been preserved!

steps.title: Add: spread + new element
steps.explanation: [...nums, 4] copies the original and creates a new array with 4 appended.

steps.title: Remove: filter()
steps.explanation: filter() returns a new array containing only elements that match the condition.

steps.title: Transform: map()
steps.explanation: map() returns a new array with each element transformed.
steps.keyInsight: Use map() instead of modifying with a for loop

quiz.question: Why is immutability important in React?
options: It makes change detection easy (reference comparison)
quiz.explanation:
With immutability, you can detect changes by comparing references alone.
If you mutate objects directly, you lose track of the previous state and must compare everything.

misconceptions.wrong: Immutability is slow (because it copies every time)
misconceptions.correct: Shallow copying is fast, and the optimization gained from change detection can improve overall performance.
misconceptions.why: Libraries like React leverage immutability to render efficiently.

keyTakeaway: Immutability = copy instead of mutate, essential pattern for React/Redux
